Change c0082. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. III; 1831 Ch. IV.

Context before (unchanged): When I had arrived at this point, and had become as well acquainted with the theory and practice of natural philosophy as depended on the lessons of any of the professors at Ingolstadt, my residence there being no longer conducive to my improvements, I thought of returning to my friends and my native town, when an incident happened that protracted my stay.

1818 text: One of the phænonema which had peculiarly attracted my attention was the structure of the human frame, and, indeed, any animal endued with life.

1831 text: One of the phenomena which had peculiarly attracted my attention was the structure of the human frame, and, indeed, any animal endued with life.

Diff: One of the [-phænonema-] {+phenomena+} which had peculiarly attracted my attention was the structure of the human frame, and, indeed, any animal endued with life.

Context after (unchanged): Whence, I often asked myself, did the principle of life proceed?

result.rationale: Only the orthography changes: 'phænonema' becomes 'phenomena' (the ligature æ is dropped and the spelling corrected). The wording, meaning and sentence structure are untouched.
